INTRODUCTION

Welcome to Your Comprehensive Scheme of Work Resource
About This Ebook

Welcome to this comprehensive collection of Schemes of Work for Pre-primary and Primary
education, covering the complete educational journey from Prenursery through Primary 6
(ages 2-12 years). This resource provides detailed, term-by-term curriculum guidance for all
essential subjects across all class levels.


Official Curriculum Alignment

This Scheme of Work is fully aligned with Nigerian educational authorities:

FOR PRIMARY EDUCATION (Primary 1-6): Completely aligned with the Nigerian
Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC) - the Federal Government's
curriculum authority - ensuring full compliance with national standards, learning objectives,
and assessment frameworks.

FOR EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION (Prenursery - Nursery 3): Fully aligned with
the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools (NAPPS) curriculum
framework, meeting recognized standards for quality pre-primary education.

This dual alignment ensures regulatory compliance, quality assurance, and confidence for
administrators, teachers, parents, and educational authorities.


Coverage

PRE-PRIMARY (NAPPS-Aligned): Prenursery, Nursery 1, 2, 3

PRIMARY (NERDC-Aligned): Primary 1-6

ALL ESSENTIAL SUBJECTS

The 13-Week Structure

Each term follows this proven format:

      Weeks 1-4: New content introduction
      Week 5: Mid-term Assessment
      Week 6: Mid-term Break
      Weeks 7-10: Advanced content
      Week 11: Comprehensive Revision

                                            6 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
        GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




       Week 12: End of Term Examination
       Week 13: Closing & Awards


Key Features

✓ Officially Compliant - Meets NERDC and NAPPS standards

✓ Age-Appropriate - Content matched to developmental stages

✓ Comprehensive - Complete curriculum coverage

✓ Detailed - Week-by-week guidance with full content breakdown

✓ Progressive - Logical skill building from simple to complex

✓ Practical - Ready for immediate classroom implementation

✓ Holistic - Academic, social, emotional, physical, and moral development

✓ Flexible - Adaptable while maintaining curriculum requirements


Getting Started

   1.   Select your class level
   2.   Review the complete term structure
   3.   Prepare necessary resources
   4.   Implement with confidence knowing you are meeting all official requirements
   5.   Track progress against national standards
   6.   Celebrate achievements


Our Commitment

These schemes represent a commitment to both educational excellence and full regulatory
compliance. Every topic has been carefully planned to ensure children receive quality
education while schools meet all NERDC (Primary) and NAPPS (Early Childhood)
requirements.

From Prenursery to Primary 6, this ebook provides structured guidance that transforms
classrooms while satisfying regulatory standards.

Welcome to structured excellence in education—where quality meets compliance!

                                dirty water clean and safe to drink

                               496 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT

      PURIFICATION             -Why purify water: remove dirt, kill germs,
                               prevent diseases
                               - Methods of water purification:
                               *Boiling: heating water until it bubbles, kills
                               germs (most common method at home)
                                * Filtration: passing water through filter to
                               remove dirt
                               *Adding chemicals: water purification tablets,
                               chlorine (in treated water)
                               *Settling and decanting: letting dirt settle,
                               pouring clean water off top
                               - Importance of drinking clean water only
                               - Understanding tap water is usually treated
2     WATER: STORAGE           -Importance of proper water storage: keeps
                               water clean, prevents contamination
                               - Safe water storage containers: covered
                               buckets, jerry cans, water tanks, bottles
                               -Properties of good storage containers: clean,
                               covered (to keep out dirt and insects), made of
                               safe materials
                               -Storage practices: washing containers before
                               use, keeping containers covered always, storing
                               in clean place, not touching water with dirty
                               hands
                               -Understanding stored water can become dirty
                               if not protected
                               - Regular cleaning of storage containers
3     WATER-BORNE DISEASES     - Understanding water-borne diseases:
                               sicknesses caused by dirty water or germs in
                               water
                               -Common water-borne diseases: diarrhea,
                               cholera, typhoid fever, dysentery
                               -How diseases spread through water: drinking
                               dirty water, eating food washed with dirty
                               water, not washing hands
                               -Symptoms: stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhea
                               (frequent watery stool), weakness, fever
                               -Prevention: drinking only clean/boiled water,
                               washing hands with soap, keeping water
                               covered, proper toilet use
                               -Treatment: see doctor immediately, drink
                               plenty of clean water (ORS - Oral Rehydration
                               Solution)
                               - Understanding prevention is better than cure

      HOW TO TAKE CARE      daily with soap and water, brushing teeth twice

                            -Importance of body care: prevents diseases, keeps

                              - Consequences of poor dental care: tooth decay,

WEEK TOPIC                  CONTENT
1     DISPOSAL OF REFUSE:   -Understanding refuse: waste materials we throw
      SAFE AND UNSAFE       away, garbage, rubbish
      WAYS                  -Safe/clean ways of disposing refuse: using waste
                            bins/trash cans, putting refuse in designated
                            places, tying refuse in bags before disposal, taking
                            refuse to collection points, burning in safe
                            incinerators (adults only), burying biodegradable
                            waste in proper pits
                            -Unsafe/dirty ways: throwing refuse anywhere
                            (littering), dumping in drains/gutters (causes
                            blockage and flooding), throwing in rivers/streams
                            (pollutes water), leaving refuse uncovered (attracts
                            flies, rats, mosquitoes), burning in open areas (air
                            pollution, fire hazard)
                            -Consequences of improper disposal: diseases, bad
                            smell, dirty environment, blocked drains, flooding
                            - Everyone's responsibility to dispose refuse
                            properly
2     DISPOSAL OF WASTE:    -Meaning of waste: unwanted or unusable
      MEANING AND TYPES     materials, things we no longer need
                            - Understanding waste comes from homes,
                            schools, markets, industries
                            -Types of waste: Solid waste - paper, cardboard,
                            cartons, plastic bottles, cans, food scraps, leaves,
                            wood, broken items, cloth; Liquid waste - urine,
                            dirty water from washing, drainage water, waste
                            oil, chemical liquids
                            - Other waste types: biodegradable (can
                            rot/decompose - food, leaves, paper) and non-
                            biodegradable (cannot rot - plastic, glass, metal)
                            - Proper disposal for each type
                            - Reducing waste: using less, reusing items, not
                            wasting
3     DISPOSAL OF ANIMAL    -Understanding animal waste: droppings/feces
      WASTE                 from animals, dead animals
                            -Types of animal waste: cow dung, chicken

                            -Proper disposal methods: burying animal waste in
                            pits away from water sources, using for

                             compost/fertilizer (with proper treatment),

                             clothing (leather, wool)
                             -Uses of animal waste: fertilizer for farms/gardens
                             (manure), biogas production (fuel), compost for
                             plants
                             -Importance of proper disposal: prevents diseases,

4     COMPOSTING OF          -Meaning of composting: controlled
      WASTE: MEANING,        rotting/decomposing of biodegradable waste to
      BENEFITS AND           make fertilizer (compost)
      MATERIALS              -Understanding compost: natural fertilizer made
                             from waste, looks like dark soil
                             -Benefits of composting: turns waste into useful
                             product, provides nutrients for plants, helps plants
                             grow better, reduces amount of waste, good for
                             environment, saves money (free fertilizer),
                             improves soil quality
                             -Compost materials: green materials (fresh grass,
                             vegetable scraps, fruit peels, leaves, tea bags),
                             brown materials (dry leaves, paper, cardboard,
                             sawdust, straw), water and air
                             - What NOT to compost: meat, bones, oils,

                             -Simple composting process: pile materials, keep

1     SANITATION:          -Meaning of sanitation: keeping our environment
      MEANING AND          clean and free from dirt, germs, and diseases
      IMPORTANCE           -Understanding sanitation involves proper disposal
                           of waste, clean water supply, clean toilets, drainage
                           -Importance of sanitation: prevents diseases, makes

                           breeding of flies and mosquitoes, promotes good

                           - Everyone's responsibility to maintain sanitation

      THAT NEED TO BE      bedroom, bathroom, toilet, kitchen, living room,

                           weekly (general cleaning), monthly (deep cleaning)
                           - Community sanitation days

      TO CARE FOR          high, sun is very strong, feels very warm
      ONESELF              -What to eat and drink: drink plenty of water (at

                           oranges, pineapple - lots of water in them), eat light
                           meals, avoid heavy/fatty foods, drink fresh fruit
                           juice, eat vegetables
                           -What to wear: light-colored clothes (reflect heat),
                           cotton clothes (allow air), loose clothes, hats or caps
                           (protect head from sun), sunglasses (protect eyes)
                           -Where to go/activities: stay in shade during hottest
                           hours (12pm-3pm), play in morning or evening, go

                           in afternoon
                           - Other care: use umbrella or hat when outside,

4     COLD WEATHER:        -Understanding cold weather: when temperature is
      HOW TO CARE FOR      low, feels chilly or very cold, common during
      ONESELF              harmattan or rainy season
                           -What to eat and drink: eat warm foods (soup,
                           porridge, hot meals), drink warm drinks (tea, hot
                           chocolate, warm water), eat energy-giving foods

                           - Other care: protect from cold wind, dry body

8     DISEASE AND          -Meaning of disease: illness or sickness that affects
      SICKNESS: MEANING    how body works, makes us feel unwell
      AND EXAMPLES         -Understanding difference between disease (specific
                           illness) and sickness (general feeling unwell)
                           -Examples of common diseases: Skin diseases -
                           rashes, ringworm, scabies, eczema; Stomach

                           fever; Parasitic diseases - malaria (from

                           -Symptoms vary by disease: fever, pain, weakness,

9     WATER-BORNE          - Understanding water-borne diseases: diseases
      DISEASES             caused by drinking dirty/contaminated water or
                           contact with dirty water
                           -Common water-borne diseases: Cholera - severe
                           diarrhea and vomiting, dehydration; Typhoid fever -
                           high fever, stomach pain, headache; Dysentery -
                           bloody diarrhea, stomach cramps; Diarrhea -
                           frequent watery stool, stomach pain; Guinea worm -
                           worm in body from drinking contaminated water;
                           Hepatitis A - liver disease, yellow eyes and skin
                           -How diseases spread: drinking dirty water, eating
                           food washed with dirty water, not washing hands,
                           swimming in contaminated water
                           -Symptoms: diarrhea, vomiting, fever, stomach
                           pain, weakness
                           - Prevention: drink only clean/boiled water, wash
                           hands with soap, keep water covered, use clean
                           water for cooking, proper toilet use
                           - Treatment: see doctor immediately, drink plenty of

                            safe water (ORS), take prescribed medicine
10     AIR-BORNE DISEASES   Air-borne diseases:
       & PREVENTION AND     -Understanding air-borne diseases: spread through
       TREATMENT            air when sick person coughs, sneezes, or breathes
                            -Common air-borne diseases: Common cold - runny
                            nose, cough, sneezing; Influenza (flu) - fever, cough,
                            body ache, headache; Tuberculosis (TB) - persistent
                            cough, chest pain, weight loss; Measles - fever, rash,
                            cough, red eyes; Chicken pox - fever, itchy
                            spots/blisters; Whooping cough - severe coughing
                            fits; Mumps - swollen cheeks and jaw
                            - How diseases spread: breathing same air as sick
                            person, coughing/sneezing without covering mouth,
                            close contact with sick person

                            Prevention and Treatment:
                            -Prevention: covering mouth when
                            coughing/sneezing, washing hands frequently,
                            avoiding close contact with sick people, keeping
                            environment clean, good ventilation (fresh air),
                            immunization/vaccination, eating healthy food
                            (strong immune system), getting enough rest
                            -Treatment: seeing doctor, taking prescribed
                            medicine, resting, drinking plenty of fluids, eating
                            nutritious food, staying away from others to prevent
                            spread, completing medication course

                           - Understanding abuse is wrong and harmful

                           - Understanding abuse is never the child's fault
                           -Basic understanding that abuse violates children's

                           - Difference between discipline and abuse
                           -Understanding children should feel safe at home,
                           school, and everywhere
                           - Knowing abuse should be reported to trusted adults

      ABUSE                causing physical injury

                           - Neglect: not providing food, clothes, shelter,

                           excessive work instead of going to school

                           - Bullying: repeated hurting by other children

PHYSICAL AND HEALTH EDUCATION SCHEME OF WORK (NURSERY 3)
FIRST TERM

WEEK TOPIC                   CONTENT
1     EXERCISES AND GAMES:   -Understanding what exercise means: physical
      IMPORTANCE             activities that make our body move and work
                             -Understanding what games are: organized
                             activities with rules, usually for fun and
                             competition
                             -Importance of exercises and games: keeps body
                             strong and healthy, helps us grow properly,
                             develops muscles and bones, improves flexibility
                             and balance, gives us energy, helps heart and
                             lungs work better, prevents obesity (being
                             overweight), makes us happy and reduces stress,
                             helps us sleep better, teaches discipline and focus,
                             develops social skills through team games,
                             improves coordination, builds confidence
                             -Understanding regular physical activity is
                             essential for children
                             - Exercise should be fun, not punishment
2     GAMES: BASIC GAMES     - Introduction to simple competitive games
                             -Egg and Spoon Race: balancing object (often
                             bean bag or small ball) on spoon while racing,
                             teaches balance and control, can't let object fall
                             -Sack Race: jumping in sack/bag to finish line,
                             teaches coordination and leg strength, fun
                             competitive activity
                             -Blindfold and Fill a Basket: blindfolded player
                             tries to pick up objects and put in basket (with
                             guidance from teammates), teaches trust,
                             listening skills, spatial awareness
                             -Other games: three-legged race (two people's
                             legs tied together), musical chairs, freeze dance,
                             obstacle course
                             - Understanding rules of each game
                             - Fair play and sportsmanship
                             - Taking turns and encouraging others
3     BODY EXERCISE:         -Stretching exercises: reaching for sky (arms
      STRETCHING, BENDING,   up), touching toes, side stretches, neck rolls, arm
      RAISING ARMS AND       circles, ankle rotations
      LEGS, SKIPPING         -Importance of stretching: warms up muscles,
                             prevents injuries, increases flexibility
                             - Bending exercises: bending forward, backward


                             546 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
    GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




                             (carefully), side bends, knee bends (squats)
                             -Raising arms and legs: arm raises (front, side,
                             up), leg raises (marching, side leg lifts, back leg
                             lifts), developing strength and control
                             -Skipping: jumping with rope (forward,
                             backward), jumping without rope, counting skips
                             -Benefits: improves coordination, cardiovascular
                             fitness, leg strength
                             - Proper form and safety in all exercises
4     BODY EXERCISE:         -Leaping: big jumps from one foot to the other
      LEAPING AND HOPPING    foot, covering distance, arm movements while
                             leaping, leaping over small obstacles (lines,
                             cones), leaping in different directions (forward,
                             sideways)
                             -Benefits: develops leg power, improves
                             coordination, builds confidence
                             -Hopping: jumping on one foot repeatedly,
                             hopping on right foot, hopping on left foot,
                             hopping forward and backward, hopping in
                             place, counting hops
                             -Benefits: strengthens individual legs, improves
                             balance, develops control
                             - Games incorporating leaping and hopping
                             -Understanding difference between hopping (one
                             foot) and jumping (two feet)
                             - Safety: using appropriate space, not hopping on

                              -Good sitting posture: back straight, feet flat on
                              floor, sitting back in chair, not slouching, head
                              level, shoulders relaxed
                              -Importance: prevents back pain, better
                              breathing, easier concentration, looks confident
                              - Good standing posture: standing straight,
                              shoulders back, head up, weight distributed
                              evenly on both feet, stomach in, not leaning to
                              one side
                              -Importance: prevents fatigue, looks confident,
                              better for spine health, proper body alignment
                              -Good reading posture: book at proper distance
                              (not too close), adequate lighting, sitting with
                              back support, book at eye level, not lying flat
                              while reading, taking breaks
                              -Importance: prevents eye strain, better reading,
                              prevents neck pain
                              -Good sleeping posture: sleeping on side (best)
                              or back, proper pillow height, comfortable
                              mattress, not sleeping on stomach (can strain
                              neck), relaxed position
                              -Importance: better sleep quality, prevents body
                              aches, proper spine alignment, waking refreshed

      LETTERS: e, f             starting point

                                - Tracing and independent writing

                                      - Decorative items: vases, sculptures
                                      - Children's toys

                                     •Traditional pottery in Nigeria: different ethnic
                                     groups' pottery styles

     First Aid                        someone is hurt or sick
                                      • Why first aid is important: stops pain, prevents

                                      •When we need first aid: cuts, bruises, nose

                                      • Staying calm when someone is hurt

                                      • Contents of first aid box:
                                       - Bandages and plasters (for covering cuts)
                                       - Cotton wool (for cleaning wounds)
                                       - Antiseptic liquid/cream (for cleaning cuts)
                                       - Scissors (for cutting bandages)
                                       - Thermometer (for checking temperature)
                                       - Safety pins
                                      •Where to find first aid boxes: school clinic,
                                      home, car
                                      • Never play with first aid items
                                      •Activity: Identifying first aid items, creating
                                      class first aid poster
3      First Aid: Treating Minor      • Treating small cuts and scrapes:
       Injuries (Part 1)               1. Tell an adult immediately
                                       2. Clean with clean water
                                       3. Apply antiseptic (adult does this)
                                       4. Cover with plaster or bandage
                                      • Treating bruises:
                                       - Apply cold compress (ice pack or cold cloth)
                                       - Rest the hurt part
                                      • What NOT to do:
                                       - Don't touch wound with dirty hands
                                       - Don't remove bandage too soon
                                      •Activity: Demonstrating on dolls, practicing
                                      calling for help

       Injuries (Part 2)               - Sit upright, don't lie down
                                       - Lean forward slightly

                                 - Pinch soft part of nose
                                 - Breathe through mouth

                                 - Don't scratch
                                 - Wash with soap and water
                                 - Apply cream (adult does this)
                                 - Tell adult if swelling or pain
                                • Treating minor burns (from hot water, sun):
                                 - Run cool water over burn

                                          Types of stress: Word stress: emphasis on

       (Continued)                        Two-syllable nouns/adjectives: stress first

    SAMPLE LESSON NOTE ON
PRE-NURSERY HEALTH HABITS (FIRST TERM)




                         958 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




WEEK 1: INTRODUCTION TO OUR BODY


Our body is everything that makes us. It has many parts and each part has a name.




Body Parts:
Head: This is at the top of our body. It is round. Our brain is inside our head. We wear caps
and hats on our head.
Face: This is the front part of our head. Our eyes, nose, mouth, and ears are on our face. We
use our face to smile and show our feelings.
Hands: We have two hands. Our hands help us hold things, eat food, play with toys, and
wave hello and goodbye. Each hand has five fingers.
Legs: We have two legs. Our legs help us stand, walk, run, and jump. At the end of each leg
is a foot with five toes.
Body: This means all of us together - from head to feet. Our body is special and we must take
care of it.

Why Our Body is Important:




                                            959 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




Our body helps us do many things. We use our body to play, eat, learn, and grow. Each part
works together to help us every day.

Taking Care of Our Body:
We must keep our body clean and healthy. We do this by bathing regularly, eating good food,
drinking water, and resting well. When we take care of our body, we stay strong and healthy.




EVALUATION:
   1. Point to your head
   2. Where are your hands?


                                            960 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




   3. Touch your legs
   4. Show me your face
   5. Say "body" with teacher
ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Please help your child at home by:
      Singing body parts songs together
      Pointing to and naming body parts during bath time
      Playing "touch your head/hands/legs" game
      Letting your child look in the mirror to see their body parts




                                             961 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




WEEK 2: CARE OF THE SKIN I - BATHING REGULARLY
Our skin covers our whole body. We must keep our skin clean by bathing every day.



What is Bathing?
Bathing means washing our body with water and soap. When we bathe, we clean all the dirt
from our skin. We should bathe every day to stay clean and healthy.




Things We Use for Bathing:
Water: We use clean water to wash our body. Water helps remove dirt from our skin.
Soap: Soap makes foam and bubbles. It helps clean our skin and makes us smell nice. We
rub soap on our body when bathing.

Sponge: A sponge is soft. We use it to scrub our body gently. The sponge helps the soap
clean our skin better.
Towel: After bathing, we use a towel to dry our body. The towel soaks up the water from
our skin.




                                            962 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




How We Bathe:
First, we wet our body with water. Then we apply soap and use the sponge to wash all parts
of our body - our arms, legs, chest, back, and everywhere. After washing, we rinse off the
soap with clean water. Then we dry our body with a clean towel.



Why We Should Bathe Every Day:
      To remove dirt and germs from our skin
      To keep our body clean and fresh
      To smell nice
      To stay healthy and strong
      To feel comfortable and happy
When we bathe regularly, our skin is clean, we smell good, and we feel fresh. People like to
be around children who are clean and smell nice.




                                             963 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




EVALUATION:
   1. Show how we wash our body (mime the action)
   2. Point to the soap
   3. What do we use to dry our body?
   4. When should we bathe? (Every day)
   5. Can you identify the sponge?



ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Please support your child by:

      Naming bathing materials as you use them during bath time
      Singing bathing songs while bathing your child
      Letting your child observe the bathing process
      Encouraging good bathing habits daily

WEEK 3: CARE OF THE SKIN II - APPLYING BODY CREAM
After we finish bathing, we must dry our body and apply cream. This keeps our skin soft and
healthy.




Drying Our Body:
When we finish bathing and rinse off all the soap, our body is wet. We must dry it with a
clean towel. We pat the towel gently on our skin - on our arms, legs, body, and everywhere
until we are dry. A wet body can make us feel cold, so we must dry properly.



Applying Body Cream:
After drying, we apply body cream on our skin. Body cream is also called lotion. It is smooth
and soft. We take some cream in our hands and rub it gently on our arms, legs, and body.
The cream makes our skin soft, smooth, and shiny.



Applying Hair Cream:
We also apply cream on our hair. Hair cream keeps our hair healthy, soft, and neat. It makes
our hair look nice and prevents it from being dry.



Why We Apply Cream:


                                            965 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




      To keep our skin soft and smooth
      To prevent dry skin
      To make our body look healthy and shiny
      To keep our hair neat and healthy
      To smell fresh and nice




The Complete Routine:
After bathing, we follow these steps:
   1. Dry our body with a clean towel
   2. Apply body cream all over our skin
   3. Apply hair cream on our hair
When we do this every day after bathing, our skin stays soft and our hair stays healthy. We
look clean, neat, and well taken care of.



Materials We Use:
Towel: Soft cloth to dry our body after bathing
Body Cream/Lotion: Smooth cream to make our skin soft
Hair Cream: Special cream for our hair to keep it healthy

                                             966 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




EVALUATION:
   1. What do we use to dry our body? (Towel)
   2. Show how to dry your body (mime the action)
   3. When do we apply cream? (After bathing)
   4. Pretend to apply cream on your arms
   5. Point to the body cream



ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Please help your child by:

      Showing the drying and cream application process
      Naming the items: towel, body cream, hair cream
      Letting your child help apply cream with supervision
      Making this part of the daily bathing routine

WEEK 4: CARE OF THE SKIN III - MATERIALS USED
Today we will learn about all the materials we use to take care of our skin. These materials
help us keep our body clean and healthy.



All Skin Care Materials:




1.Soap: Soap is what we use to wash our body. It can be bar soap or liquid soap. When we
mix soap with water, it makes foam and bubbles. Soap removes dirt and germs from our skin.
It makes us clean and smell nice. We use soap every time we bathe.
2.Sponge: The sponge is soft and absorbs water. We use the sponge to scrub our body when
bathing. It helps spread the soap all over our skin and cleans better. Some sponges are soft
and gentle on our skin. We squeeze the sponge to make foam with the soap.
3.Towel: The towel is made of soft cloth. We use it to dry our body after bathing. Towels
absorb water from our wet skin. We should use a clean towel each time we bathe. After using
the towel, we hang it up to dry.
4.Body Cream/Lotion: This is smooth cream that we apply on our skin after drying. It
comes in bottles or containers. Body cream keeps our skin soft and prevents it from being dry
and rough. It makes our skin smooth and shiny.
5.Hair Cream: This is special cream for our hair. It keeps our hair soft, healthy, and easy to
comb. Hair cream makes our hair look neat and shiny. We apply it after bathing when our
hair is still a bit damp.




                                             968 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




How We Use These Materials:
For bathing, we use water, soap, and sponge to wash our body clean. After rinsing, we use
the towel to dry. Then we apply body cream on our skin and hair cream on our hair. All
these materials work together to keep us clean and healthy.



Keeping Materials Clean:
We must keep our bathing materials clean:
      Rinse the soap after using it
      Squeeze out water from the sponge and let it dry
      Hang the towel to dry after use
      Close cream containers after using them
      Keep all materials in a clean place




Complete Skin Care Routine:
   1. Wet body with clean water
   2. Apply soap and use sponge to wash all body parts
   3. Rinse body with clean water to remove soap
   4. Dry body with clean towel
   5. Apply body cream on skin


                                             969 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




   6. Apply hair cream on hair
When we use all these materials properly, our skin stays clean, soft, and healthy. We look
neat and feel good about ourselves.



EVALUATION:
   1. Point to the soap when asked
   2. Which material do we use to dry our body?
   3. Match the sponge to its picture
   4. What do we use to make our skin soft? (Body cream)
   5. Name any material used for skin care

      Asking your child to identify each item
      Playing "Find the soap/towel/sponge" game
      Letting your child help arrange bathing materials
      Praising correct identification

WEEK 7: CARE OF THE MOUTH AND TEETH I - INTRODUCTION
Welcome back! Today we begin learning about another important part of our body - our
mouth and teeth.



What is the Mouth?
The mouth is the opening on our face where we eat food and talk. It is below our nose. We
open and close our mouth many times every day. Our mouth has lips on the outside and
teeth, tongue, and gums inside.




What are Teeth?
Teeth are the hard, white things inside our mouth. When we open our mouth wide and look
in a mirror, we can see our teeth. Teeth are very important. We have small teeth in the front
and bigger teeth at the back of our mouth.




                                           971 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




Why Are Teeth Important?
For Eating: Our teeth help us bite and chew our food. When we eat an apple, we bite it with
our front teeth. When we chew our food, we use our back teeth. Without teeth, we cannot
eat properly.
For Speaking: Our teeth help us talk clearly. They help us say certain words correctly. Try
saying "tooth" - your tongue touches your teeth when you say it.
For Smiling: Our teeth make our smile beautiful. When we smile, people see our white,
clean teeth. A good smile makes us look happy and friendly.

For Health: Healthy teeth mean a healthy body. When our teeth are clean and strong, we
can eat well and stay healthy.



Types of Teeth:
We have different types of teeth in our mouth, but at your age, the important thing to know
is that all our teeth are precious and we must take care of them.



Healthy Teeth vs Unhealthy Teeth:

                                             972 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




Healthy teeth are clean, white, and strong. They do not hurt. Children with healthy teeth
can eat all kinds of food without pain.
Unhealthy teeth may be dirty, have black spots, or cause pain. When we don't take care of
our teeth, they can become unhealthy and hurt us.



How to Have Healthy Teeth:
To keep our teeth healthy, we must:
      Brush them regularly
      Keep them clean
      Eat good food
      Visit the dentist when needed
Our teeth are precious. We must learn to take care of them properly so they stay white, clean,
and strong throughout our life.



EVALUATION:
   1. Point to your mouth
   2. Open your mouth and show your teeth
   3. What do teeth help us do? (Eat, talk, smile)
   4. Which picture shows healthy teeth? (Clean, white teeth)
   5. Show how you chew food



ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Please help your child by:

      Letting them look at their teeth in a mirror
      Talking about how teeth help us eat and smile
      Pointing out healthy teeth when you see smiles
      Making dental health awareness fun and positive

       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




WEEK 8: CARE OF THE MOUTH AND TEETH II - BRUSHING TWICE DAILY
Now that we know about our teeth, we must learn how to keep them clean and healthy. The
best way to care for our teeth is by brushing them regularly.




What is Tooth Brushing?
Tooth brushing means cleaning our teeth with a toothbrush and toothpaste. When we eat
food, small pieces can stick to our teeth. If we don't remove them, our teeth can become dirty
and unhealthy. Brushing helps remove food and dirt from our teeth.



How Many Times Should We Brush?
We must brush our teeth TWO times every day:
1.Morning Brushing: We brush our teeth in the morning when we wake up. Some people
brush before breakfast, others brush after breakfast. The important thing is to brush in the
morning. This removes all the dirt that stayed on our teeth while we slept.

2. Night Brushing: We brush our teeth at night before going to bed. This is very important
because it cleans our teeth before we sleep. When we sleep with clean teeth, they stay healthy.



How to Remember When to Brush:
Think about the sun and the moon:
      When the sun comes up in the morning - brush your teeth!
      When the moon comes out at night - brush your teeth!
That makes TWO times every day. We can count: "One" (morning), "Two" (night).

                                             974 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




How We Brush Our Teeth:




   1. Wet the toothbrush with water
   2. Put a tiny bit of toothpaste on the brush
   3. Brush the front of your teeth - up and down
   4. Brush the back of your teeth - up and down
   5. Brush the top parts where you chew - back and forth
   6. Brush gently - don't brush too hard
   7. Brush for a little while - not too fast
   8. Rinse your mouth with water
   9. Spit out the water and toothpaste



Why Must We Brush Twice Daily?


                                                975 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




      To remove food stuck between our teeth
      To keep our teeth white and clean
      To prevent teeth from hurting
      To keep our mouth fresh
      To prevent bad breath
      To make our smile beautiful
      To keep our teeth strong and healthy



What Happens If We Don't Brush?
If we don't brush our teeth regularly:
      Food remains on our teeth
      Teeth become dirty and yellow
      Teeth may start to hurt
      Our mouth may smell bad
      We may get tooth problems
But when we brush twice every day, our teeth stay clean, white, and healthy!



EVALUATION:
   1. Show me how to brush your teeth (mime the action)
   2. How many times do we brush? (Two times)
   3. When do we brush in the morning? (When the sun is up)
   4. When do we brush at night? (Before sleeping/when moon is out)
   5. Sing the brushing song with actions



ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Please help establish good brushing habits:
      Brush your child's teeth twice daily (morning and night)

                                              976 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
    GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




   Let your child watch you brush your teeth
   Make brushing a regular, fun routine
   Use the sun/moon reference to help them remember
   Praise your child for brushing regularly
   Be patient and encouraging

WEEK 9: CARE OF THE MOUTH AND TEETH III - USING MOUTHWASH
Besides brushing our teeth, there is another way to keep our mouth clean and fresh - using
mouthwash.

What is Mouthwash?
Mouthwash is a special liquid that helps clean our mouth. It comes in a bottle. Mouthwash
helps reach places in our mouth that the toothbrush may not clean completely. It makes our
breath smell fresh and nice.




IMPORTANT SAFETY RULE:
Mouthwash should ONLY be used with the help of your parents or guardians. Never use
mouthwash by yourself. Always ask an adult to help you.

How Mouthwash is Used (With Parent's Help):
   1. Ask your parent or guardian to help you
   2. Parent pours a little bit of mouthwash into a small cup
   3. Take the liquid into your mouth (don't swallow it!)
   4. Swish it around in your mouth - move it from side to side gently
   5. Keep it in your mouth for a few seconds
   6. Spit it out into the sink
   7. DO NOT SWALLOW the mouthwash


                                           978 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




What Does "Swish" Mean?
Swishing means moving the liquid around in your mouth. Your cheeks puff out a little and
the liquid moves all around your teeth, gums, and tongue. This helps clean all parts of your
mouth.



Why We Use Mouthwash:
      It cleans all parts of the mouth, including places the brush cannot reach
      It removes tiny pieces of food
      It makes our breath smell fresh
      It helps keep our mouth healthy and clean
      It makes our mouth feel fresh




When Do We Use Mouthwash?


                                            979 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




Mouthwash is usually used after brushing our teeth. Some families use it in the morning after
brushing, some use it at night, and some use it twice a day. Your parents will tell you when
to use it.



Safety Rules to Remember:
      Never use mouthwash without an adult's help
      Never swallow mouthwash - always spit it out
      If mouthwash gets in your eyes, tell an adult immediately
      Never play with the mouthwash bottle
      Always ask: "Mom/Dad, please help me use mouthwash"



Practice Makes Perfect:
Before using real mouthwash, we can practice the swishing and spitting action with plain
water. This helps us learn how to do it properly. Once we know how to swish and spit well,
then parents can help us use real mouthwash.



EVALUATION:
   1. Point to the mouthwash bottle
   2. Show me how to swish (move your mouth like liquid is swirling)
   3. Who should help you use mouthwash? (Parents/adults)
   4. Can you practice spitting action?
   5. Should we swallow mouthwash? (No, we spit it out)



ASSIGNMENT:
Dear Parents/Guardians,
Important information about mouthwash:
      Always supervise your child when using mouthwash
      Use child-friendly, alcohol-free mouthwash if introducing it
      Demonstrate proper swishing and spitting


                                            980 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
    GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




   Practice with plain water first
   Teach your child never to swallow mouthwash
   Consider your child's readiness - it's okay to wait until they're older

WEEK 10: CARE OF THE MOUTH AND TEETH IV - MATERIALS USED
Today we will learn about all the materials we use to take care of our mouth and teeth. Each
material has a special job in keeping our mouth clean and healthy.

All Dental Care Materials:




1.Toothbrush: The toothbrush is a small brush with soft bristles. The bristles are the tiny
soft hairs at the top of the brush. We use the toothbrush to scrub our teeth clean.
Toothbrushes come in different colors and sizes. Children should use small toothbrushes
with soft bristles that are gentle on teeth and gums. We should change our toothbrush when
the bristles become old and bent.
2.Toothpaste: Toothpaste is a special paste we put on the toothbrush. It comes in a tube.
When we squeeze the tube, toothpaste comes out. We only need a tiny bit of toothpaste -
about the size of a small pea. Toothpaste has a nice taste and smell. It makes foam when we
brush and helps clean our teeth properly. Toothpaste makes our teeth white, clean, and our
breath fresh.




                                             982 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
      GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




3.Cup: We use a small cup to hold water for rinsing our mouth. After brushing, we take
water in the cup, put it in our mouth, swish it around, and spit it out. This washes away the
toothpaste and any dirt from our teeth. We can also use the cup to hold water for wetting our
toothbrush before brushing. The cup should be clean and used only for mouth care.
4.Mouthwash: This is a special liquid in a bottle that helps clean our mouth completely. We
use it with our parent's help after brushing. Mouthwash reaches all the corners of our mouth
and makes our breath very fresh. Remember, we must never use mouthwash without an
adult's help, and we must never swallow it.



The Complete Mouth Care Routine:




Step 1: Take your toothbrush and wet it with water from the cup
Step 2: Put a tiny bit of toothpaste on the toothbrush
Step 3: Brush all your teeth - front, back, and top - up and down, back and forth, gently
Step 4: Take water in your mouth from the cup and swish it around
Step 5: Spit out the water and toothpaste into the sink
Step 6: Rinse your mouth again with clean water to make sure all toothpaste is out
Step 7: With parent's help, use mouthwash if needed - swish and spit
Step 8: Rinse your toothbrush and cup with clean water
Step 9: Put everything back in its place
Step 10: Smile and show your clean, healthy teeth!


                                             983 | 985|BACK TO TABLE OF CONTENT
       GET ACCESS TO MORE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES - CLICK HERE




Taking Care of Dental Materials:
We must take care of our dental care materials:
      Rinse the toothbrush after use and let it dry standing up
      Close the toothpaste tube after using it
      Wash the cup with clean water after use
      Keep the mouthwash bottle closed
      Store all materials in a clean, dry place
      Don't share your toothbrush with anyone
Remembering the Routine:
Remember to use these materials TWICE every day - in the morning and at night before bed.
When we brush twice daily with these materials, our teeth stay white, strong, and healthy.
Our smile becomes beautiful and our mouth stays fresh all day.



EVALUATION:
   1. Point to the toothbrush
   2. What do we put on the toothbrush? (Toothpaste)
   3. Show me the cup
   4. Match each material to its picture
   5. Can you show the complete tooth brushing routine?
   6. Which materials are used to care for teeth?

      Review all dental materials with your child daily
      Let your child identify each item before use
      Practice the complete routine together
      Ask questions: "Where is your toothbrush?" "What is this?"
      Maintain the twice-daily brushing schedule
